content.text:
H2 as written doesn't fit the data, but a two-planet model with the second planet near 11.3 d instead of 1.74 d does. Its scatter is under the limit and its residuals show no significant signal.

**H2 as written (fit F2): not supported**
- **Planet 1:** period 15.28 d, amplitude 38.97 m/s, eccentricity 0.12.
- **Planet 2:** period 1.72 d, amplitude 14.95 m/s, eccentricity 0.80. The fit flagged this eccentricity as stuck at its upper limit (0.8), which usually means the period is wrong.
- **Scatter:** 11.85 m/s, limit 4.37 m/s, so it fails.
- **BIC:** 1338.6 (lower is better). The one-planet fit F1 scored 1690.8, with scatter 13.80 m/s.
- **Residual peaks:**
  - 10.40 d, false-alarm probability 3.5e-7 (threshold 1%).
  - 6.53 d, false-alarm probability 0.3%.
  - The ~1.7 d signal does not show up as a significant peak.

**Best second period from the residuals of the 15.15 d fit (F1)**
- 10.40 d, power 0.60, false-alarm probability 2.7e-11. This is clearly real.
- 6.39 d, false-alarm probability 0.19%. This is also below 1%; it may be leakage from the 10.40 d signal.
- 1.72 d has a false-alarm probability of 53%, so it is not supported.

**Corrected hypothesis H5 (15.15 d + 10.40 d), best fit F4**
I registered H5 because the flag pointed to a wrong starting period. The first fit (F3) had planet 1 stuck on its search bound at 16.67 d. F4 is the refit with the period search widened from ±10% to ±25%, and it has no flags.
- **Planet 1:** period 16.87 d, amplitude 41.79 m/s, eccentricity 0.11.
- **Planet 2:** period 11.34 d, amplitude 23.12 m/s, eccentricity 0.09.
- **Scatter:** 3.55 m/s, limit 4.37 m/s, so it passes. Reduced chi-squared is 1.80.
- **BIC:** 389.4 (lower is better). That is about 949 below H2 and about 1301 below H1; a difference of 10 or more is decisive.
- **Strongest residual peak:** 2.82 d, false-alarm probability 5.9% (threshold 1%), so not significant. It is linked as a harmonic to 1.45 d and 1.39 d. The next peak is 2.55 d at 9.7%.

**Caveat:** both periods moved a long way in F4. The outer planet went from 15.15 d to 16.87 d, and the inner one from 10.40 d to 11.34 d. The observations span only 37.25 d, so the periods are loosely pinned down. More observations would help confirm them before submitting.

Fits F2, F3 and F4 and hypothesis H5 are now in the shared lab record. I didn't add or remove any planets beyond correcting H2's second period; whether to adopt H5 is your call.
